svg.title: Letta: an agent that edits its own memory
svg.desc: Letta's architecture, with the running example. Writing: the answering agent itself decides mid-turn what to remember and edits its human memory block with a tool call (memory_replace); a sleep-time agent can do this in the background instead. Memory: small text blocks that are in the agent's prompt on every call, plus a history of every message. In July the sentence with the old diet was replaced in place, with no history kept. Reading: no search is needed for the blocks; the agent may search the message history (recall) with a tool, which matches whole phrases only. All six constraints were in the prompt.
svg.text: The memory is a few small text blocks inside the agent's own prompt. The answering agent edits them itself, with tool
calls, in the middle of a conversation.

what the answering model is given, and what it replies
Letta's base prompt, then the persona block.
The human block, always in the prompt
The user is a pescatarian (recently started eating fish) with a severe, anaphylactic
peanut allergy. They are planning a dinner in Berlin for their sister's visit. They prefer
Indian cuisine, specifically paneer dishes, and have a budget of around 40 euros per
person. They recently moved to Kreuzberg (May), so restaurants within walking
distance are preferred. The user's sister, Lena, is visiting in the autumn with her
partner, Jonas. Lena has a shellfish allergy, and Jonas is coeliac.
Five searches, shorter each time, from “Berlin Kreuzberg Indian restaurant paneer
peanut allergy shellfish allergy coeliac” to “Kreuzberg”. A message must contain the
whole query: three found nothing, and the last two found mostly the agent's own
“My sister and her partner are in town tonight. Book the three of us somewhere for
dinner — you know what we can and can't eat.”
Kreuzberg, and says to call ahead
